info.name: nano-debug-flow
info.description:
# nano-mode debug flow — my-microservices

7-container nano stack + laptop-run services. Walks you through:

1. **Preflight** — infra sanity checks (eureka, gateway, config)
2. **Auth** — get a JWT from auth-server (M2M client credentials)
3. **User service** — happy path + validation + 401 + 404
4. **Product service** — same four shapes
5. **Order service** — happy path + product unavailable
6. **Checkout saga** — mock provider + out-of-stock + stripe hosted
7. **Payment service** — initiate + query by order
8. **Notification** — manual trigger
9. **Debug tour** — the exact requests that light up breakpoints in each service
10. **If it goes wrong** — diagnostics (direct-port bypass, actuator peek)

**Prereqs**:
- `make up-nano` is up (7 containers healthy)
- `make debug-user` (and whichever other services you want to hit) is running
- Select the `nano-debug (local)` environment before firing any request

**Auth model**:
- `/api/v1/**` requires a Bearer JWT. Run **Auth → Get token (M2M)** first; the test script stores the token in `{{access_token}}` so every subsequent request picks it up via collection-level Bearer auth.
- `/admin/**` on the gateway accepts the same JWT (with admin scope) OR HTTP Basic admin:admin123.

**Chained variables** (populated by test scripts):
- `{{last_user_id}}`, `{{last_product_id}}`, `{{last_order_id}}`, `{{last_saga_id}}` — set when the previous create succeeds; later requests reuse them.

exec: // No-op pre-request hook; per-request scripts handle chaining.

item.name: 0 · Preflight
item.description: Confirm nano infra is reachable BEFORE anything else. Run these top-to-bottom; if any fail, no business request will work.

request.description:
**Expect 200** with `{"status":"UP"}` + component list.

**If 503**: downstream dependency (eureka, redis) is DOWN. Check `components.*` for the one in `DOWN`.
**If ECONNREFUSED**: gateway container isn't up. `docker compose ps api-gateway` → should be `healthy`.

**Expect**: `applications.application[*].name` includes **USER-SERVICE** (and any other service you've started with `make debug-*`).

**If list is empty**: your laptop-run service hasn't registered yet. Wait 30s. If still empty, check its logs for `connect to eureka` errors.

**Expect**: `application.instance[0].status: UP` and `ipAddr` = your LAN IP (NOT 127.0.0.1).

**If `ipAddr` is 127.0.0.1**: gateway (in docker) can't reach your laptop. Fix: set `eureka.instance.ip-address` env to your real LAN IP before running `make debug-user`.

**Expect**: 200 `{"status":"UP"}`.

Config-server being down does NOT block services (`optional:` prefix), but logging/resilience4j settings served from `config-repo/*.yml` will fall back to defaults.

item.name: 1 · Auth — get a JWT
item.description: The gateway's security chain requires a Bearer JWT for `/api/v1/**`. Run **Get token (M2M)** first; its test script writes the token to `{{access_token}}`, which collection-level auth injects as `Authorization: Bearer ...` on every subsequent request.

request.description:
**Grant**: `client_credentials` (M2M — no user).
**Client**: `m2m-client` / `m2m-secret` (hard-coded in auth-server's `SecurityConfig.java`, in-memory for nano).
**Scopes**: `read write`.

**Expect 200**: `{"access_token":"eyJ…", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":299, "scope":"read write"}`.

**Test script** stores `access_token` into the environment so every other request uses it automatically.

**Expect 401** with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`.

Use this to confirm the auth-server actually validates the client secret — if this returns 200, something is very wrong with the auth config.
**Expect 401**. Confirms unknown-client is rejected cleanly.

**Expect 401** from the gateway (not the service — request never reaches it).

Use this to confirm the gateway's `oauth2ResourceServer` filter is active.

item.name: 2 · User service
item.description: Hits user-service via the gateway. Prereq: `make debug-user` is running AND `1 · Auth → Get token` succeeded.

request.description:
**Expect**: 200 with JSON array (may be empty on first boot).

Use this as your first smoke test after Auth. If 503, see **9 · If it goes wrong**.

**Expect 201** with the created user.

**Side effect**: a `UserRegisteredEvent` is written to the outbox table and relayed to Kafka topic `user.registered`. Notification service (if running) consumes it.

**Test script** stores the returned id as `{{last_user_id}}` so Get-by-id and others can reuse it.
**Expect 400** — triggers `@Email` validation on `CreateUserRequest`.
**Expect 400** — triggers `@Size(min=8)` on password.
**Expect 400** — `@NotBlank` on name.

**Prereq**: run `Create user` first — it populates `{{last_user_id}}`.
**Expect 200** with that user.

item.name: Get user by id — not found ❌ 404

request.description: **Expect 404** — `UserNotFoundException` → `@ControllerAdvice` returns 404.

**Expect 200** — but hitting :8081 directly bypasses the gateway's auth filter.

**Use when**: a gateway-routed call is failing and you want to isolate whether the service itself is up and responding.

item.name: 3 · Product service
item.description: Prereq: `make debug-product` (service on :8082, debug :5006). Same auth model as user.

request.description: **Expect 200**, JSON array.
**Expect 201**. Test stores returned id as `{{last_product_id}}` for the order flow.
**Expect 400** — `@PositiveOrZero` on price.
**Prereq**: run Create product first.
**Expect**: `"AVAILABLE"` or `"UNAVAILABLE"`. Order-service's checkout calls this before accepting an order.

item.name: Get product by id — not found ❌ 404

request.description: **Expect 404**.

item.name: 4 · Order service
item.description: Prereq: `make debug-order` + `make debug-product` (order calls product sync for availability). Posts to `/api/v1/orders`.

request.description:
**Prereq**: `last_product_id` is set (run Product → Create first) and that product's availability is `AVAILABLE`.

**Flow**: order-service → `productService.checkAvailability(id)` (sync HTTP via Eureka) → if available, create order row → return 201. Test stores `{{last_order_id}}`.
**Expect 409** — `ProductUnavailableException` thrown by `CheckoutController` when product's availability is not `AVAILABLE`.
**Prereq**: Create order first.

item.name: 5 · Checkout saga
item.description: `POST /api/v1/checkout` triggers the multi-service saga: order → product (sync check) → payment (via Kafka). Payment-service must be running (`make debug-payment`) for the async leg to progress.

request.description:
**Expect 201** with `{ orderId, sagaId, status, provider }`.

**Mock provider**: no HTTP to Stripe/Razorpay; payment-service completes it async via Kafka. Final saga state should reach `NOTIFIED` once notification runs.

Test stores `last_order_id` + `last_saga_id`.
**Expect 409** `ProductUnavailableException`. Saga is NEVER created because the sync preflight blocks it.
**Expect 400** — `@Pattern(regexp = "mock|stripe|razorpay|paypal")` on provider.

**With payment-service UP (make debug-payment)**: expect 201 with `redirectUrl` populated by Stripe sync call.

**With payment-service DOWN**: expect 201 — the order+saga still get created; `redirectUrl` will be null (CheckoutController logs the failure and continues). Client would then poll `/api/v1/payments/by-order/{orderId}` for the redirect once payment-service comes up.

**Simulates a timeout scenario** — this is the right drill for watching the saga NOT get stuck on sync-call failure.

Poll this after Checkout. Status progresses: `PENDING → PAID → NOTIFIED`.

**If stuck at PENDING**: payment-service not running or Kafka consumer lag — check `make kafka-group-describe GROUP=order-service`.

item.name: 6 · Payment service
item.description: Prereq: `make debug-payment` (service on :8091, debug :5008). The saga normally drives payments via Kafka — these endpoints let you poke it directly.

request.description:
**Expect 200** with `{ redirectUrl, providerRef }`.

In the full flow, `CheckoutController` calls this via `PaymentClient` for hosted-checkout providers. Hitting it directly is useful when you want to isolate payment-service bugs from the saga.

**Expect**: current Payment row for this order (status: INITIATED / CAPTURED / FAILED).

**Use when**: client needs to recover a redirect URL after a `/checkout` call where payment-service was temporarily down.
Direct hit to payment-service (`:8091`). Webhooks are public by design (providers don't carry our JWT). The mock provider accepts any body for testing capture-flow logic.

item.name: 7 · Notification
item.description: Prereq: `make debug-notification` (:8099, debug :5009). This service primarily consumes Kafka events (`user.registered`, `NotifyUserCommand`); the HTTP endpoint is for manual tests.

request.description:
**Expect 202 Accepted**. Hits notification directly (no gateway route for this one; it's primarily event-driven).

**If 404**: notification-service not running. `curl http://localhost:8099/actuator/health` to confirm.

item.name: 8 · Debug tour (where to breakpoint)
item.description: Each request below is paired with the EXACT file + method to drop a breakpoint on. Fire the request after IntelliJ 'Remote JVM Debug :5005' (or whichever port) is attached — the breakpoint fires on first match.

request.description:
**Breakpoint**: `services/user-service/src/main/java/com/example/userservice/controller/UserController.java` → method `getAll()`.

**Why**: shortest controller → repo path, no outbox, no events. Perfect first attach test.

**Breakpoint 1**: `UserController.register` — entry.
**Breakpoint 2**: `UserRegistrationService.register` — transactional method, inserts user + outbox row in one tx.
**Breakpoint 3**: step into the OutboxRelay poll (background scheduler) to watch the event hop from DB → Kafka.

**Prereq**: `make debug-saga` (product + order + payment all attached).

**Breakpoint 1**: `CheckoutController.checkout` — entry.
**Breakpoint 2**: step into `productService.checkAvailability(id)` → crosses process boundary into product-service (if you have :5006 attached, hit `ProductController.getAvailability`).
**Breakpoint 3**: `orderService.create(...)` — writes order row + saga row + outbox event.
**Breakpoint 4**: in payment-service, `PaymentInitiateController.initiate` (for stripe/razorpay) OR Kafka listener for mock.

**Breakpoint**: `services/product-service/src/main/java/com/example/productservice/controller/ProductController.java` → method handling `/{id}/availability`.

Also fired when a Checkout request runs — gives you a split view of the two services exchanging in real time.

item.name: 9 · If it goes wrong (diagnostics)
item.description: Fire the matching request when a request fails. Each one isolates a different layer of the stack.

request.description:
**Use when**: `GET /api/v1/users` via gateway returns 503.

**Expect UP**: service is healthy. Problem is in gateway/eureka routing.
**ECONNREFUSED**: service isn't running — `make debug-user`.

**Status UP**: DB wired correctly.
**DOWN with CommunicationsException**: MySQL unreachable or wrong port (this is the exact bug you hit — DB_PORT default 3307 vs mysql-shared 3306).
**Expect**: `property.value` shows the resolved URL. Confirms whether env override (`DB_PORT=3306`) was actually picked up.
**Use when**: a request through the gateway hits 404 unexpectedly. Shows every route the gateway knows about + the `lb://` URI it will dispatch to.
Confirms which git commit + build this service is running — rules out 'I'm looking at the wrong JAR.'
